isolated_hypothesis: Twenty steps of bounded medium load transfer before the existing RR swing, followed by release and monotonic frozen-reference YZ endpoint tracking, can create the missing rear contact transition.

evidence.finding: Both rear wheels remained above the unchanged 8 N contact threshold for all 40 probe steps. RR moved only 2.96 mm in the required world-Y direction. FL contact fraction fell to 0.5, base orientation RMSE rose to 0.24166 rad, and relative base displacement reached [-42.56,-64.72,-18.53] mm.

reference_step_evidence.interpretation: The formal 300-step wheel error is the repeated accumulation of missed frozen-reference rear steps, not a single late disturbance.

decision_reasons: Extending the pre-load interval from nine to twenty steps did not change rear contact topology.
The resulting RR endpoint motion remained less than one tenth of the frozen-reference step while front support and pose exceeded unchanged formal limits.
No forced load-transfer or Cartesian intervention tested in attempts 158 through 160 has a safe local basin that can be promoted to expert collection.
next_action: Stop forced-output intervention development. Produce a consolidated reachability and qualification-blocker report from the complete attempt history, then retain the valid 9x100 result while keeping R0 blocked until a controller can demonstrate an actual 36 to 39 mm low-load rear step under the frozen contracts.
